event.hazel_heart2.0.text: Shh. Back here, behind Natural History. (Two visitors a year come this far. Both are me.)
event.hazel_heart2.0.why: funnier census; drops 'That's the point', which duplicated my shipped daily line

event.hazel_heart2.1.text: An almanac, eighty-one years old. Page two hundred and four: a snowdrop, still white.
event.hazel_heart2.1.why: the miracle lands last: still white

event.hazel_heart2.3.text: Beside it, in pencil: the first frost, guessed. They missed by three days. (I checked.)
event.hazel_heart2.3.why: '(I checked.)' is me; the unknown pencil hand becomes the thread

event.hazel_heart2.2.text: The reading nook. One chair. (I counted the people I'd show it to. You're the list.)
event.hazel_heart2.2.why: 'You're the list' says the heart without stating it

event.hazel_heart2.4.text: A fresh snowdrop, for you. Press it somewhere worthy. (Not the almanac. That page is taken.)
event.hazel_heart2.4.why: callback to page two hundred and four closes the scene's loop

event.hazel_heart5.0.text: I wrote you something. (Draft five. The first four are under the desk, ashamed.)
event.hazel_heart5.0.why: the drafts get a feeling; funniest word last

event.hazel_heart5.1.text: A small poem. Six lines. If you must laugh, laugh at line four. (It knows.)
event.hazel_heart5.1.why: '(It knows.)' is tighter and sadder than explaining the weak line

event.hazel_heart5.2.text: You read all six lines. (I watched. Rude of me. I don't regret it.)
event.hazel_heart5.2.why: owns the watching instead of reporting it

event.reading_night.1.text: (It doesn't.) There's a poem in my sleeve. (It's been there three days. Deciding.)
event.reading_night.1.why: the poem gets the verb; three days is more specific than 'haven't decided'

dlg.reading.hazel.r1.text: Borrowed, then. Kinder to the room. (Mine keeps my sleeve warm another night.)
dlg.reading.hazel.r1.why: the sleeve stays a character; 'another night' points forward

event.festival_winter_lanterns.1.text: One lantern, one wish. Fold it small. (Spoken wishes don't rise. I've charted this.)
event.festival_winter_lanterns.1.why: almanac-flavored superstition; 'charted' is my kind of evidence

event.hazel_heart4.intro.text: I'd like to trade. A book for a book. (Or for anything. I'm flexible about your half.)
event.hazel_heart4.intro.why: the flexibility joke replaces the apologetic 'Is that odd?'

dlg.hazel.swap.r2.text: Thank you for saying so. (Most people pretend.) I'll start you on the heron book. It's short and forgiving.
dlg.hazel.swap.r2.why: the heron becomes a real recommendation, not a stray detail

event.hazel_heart4.after.text: I'll look after it. Return date: whenever. (There is no stamp for whenever. I may need to carve one.)
event.hazel_heart4.after.why: the missing stamp makes 'whenever' concrete and earned

dlg.hazel.hiding.0.text: The festival wants a reader. Ione said my name. (An hour ago. I've alphabetized the hour away.)
dlg.hazel.hiding.0.why: the hiding becomes an activity; specific beats 'is that strange?'

event.hazel_friend.fallback.text: Blackberries, when you can. (It's waited forty-one years. One more day won't show.)
event.hazel_friend.fallback.why: repeats the forty-one; I count, so the echo is in character

event.hazel_birthday.intro.text: It's my birthday. (I kept it quiet. The cake betrayed me.) Please sit. There's enough for two.
event.hazel_birthday.intro.why: 'the cake betrayed me' is the joke 'Ione told the cake' was reaching for

event.overheard_hazel_ione_1.l1.text: Your spring almanac. Behind the mysteries, third shelf. (Someone sorted those by color. I'm coping.)
event.overheard_hazel_ione_1.l1.why: 'I'm coping' is a whole fine, unissued

event.overheard_hazel_ione_3.l2.text: Oh. (Green. My favorite. You knew.) I'm saying nothing. Loudly.
event.overheard_hazel_ione_3.l2.why: 'saying nothing, loudly' is the thank-you she can manage

event.overheard_dorian_hazel_1.l2.text: Dorian. (A whole word today. Chatty.) The bench has room, if you like.
event.overheard_dorian_hazel_1.l2.why: gentle tease at the silence, not at him; invitation kept

event.overheard_dorian_hazel_2.l2.text: Pressed leaves. May I borrow it? (This year's found bookmarks: two receipts, a sock, one apology.)
event.overheard_dorian_hazel_2.l2.why: the found-bookmark list is truer librarian comedy; the apology points at the anonymous notes

event.overheard_wren_hazel_1.l4.text: The clasp. (I wrote down all three versions. Yours are gaining.)
event.overheard_wren_hazel_1.l4.why: 'yours are gaining' admits she loves the embellishments

adds.text: You may use it when I'm shelving. (I'll hear the pages. That's enough company.)
adds.why: turns the nook from a secret into a standing invitation; seeds the second chair

threads.hazel_heart8: Who the reckless second listener will someday be.
threads.hazel_heart10: Whether the poem really hangs on a lantern at the winter festival, and who reads it there.

threads.hazel_birthday: What Hazel wrote in the margin of today, in ink she never uses.

threads.hazel_partners: What amendment the penciled name at the bottom of the page is waiting for.

threads.overheard_hazel_ione_2: Which book Hazel has reread yearly for seven years, and why she never finishes it.
threads.overheard_hazel_ione_3: Whether the lump in the cushion gets fixed before anyone admits the window chair is Hazel's.
threads.overheard_dorian_hazel_1: What a book for not reading is for.
threads.overheard_dorian_hazel_2: Whose apology was left in a returned book.
threads.overheard_dorian_hazel_3: Whether the window seat facing the forest becomes a standing appointment.
threads.overheard_wren_hazel_1: What Hazel's notebook of Wren's three versions is for.
threads.overheard_wren_hazel_2: One line read aloud at the corner stool, possibly by spring.
threads.overheard_hazel_piper_1: Who else's rhymes the neat pencil has quietly improved.
threads.overheard_hazel_piper_2: What Hazel does every Thursday behind a very large book.

notes: Canon: my bible says heart 8 is a rehearsal for the player's farm animals; the built scene is the library with the gray cat. I kept the build (the cat leaving at line three is better), but the bible should be updated to match.
hazel_courtship and hazel_courtship2 share the dialogue graph hazel.courtship; every key in it serves both scenes, so my keeps there are deliberate and apply to both.

hazel_friend's forty-one-year borrower gets a knock on a living door, so this mystery must never merge with Edmund Fenn's forty years; players will try to connect the numbers, and the near-miss is better left a coincidence.
Removed 'That's the point' from heart2.0; it duplicated my shipped daily line word for word.
Request to Ione: reading_night ends on her fifth chair and open door; I'd love a later library scene to pay that off.
